title: Python
subtitle: Beyond the basics: the data model, iteration, functions, classes and types, the tools and tests of real projects, concurrency and performance, as experienced Python programmers use them.
description: Python is a general-purpose, dynamically typed language first released by Guido van Rossum in 1991. It is known for code that reads almost like pseudocode and for a very large standard library and package ecosystem, and it is used for scripting and automation, web back ends, data analysis, scientific computing, teaching, and most of today's machine-learning research and tooling.

The Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) already teaches programming basics in Python, so this course does not. It is for people who can write small Python programs (variables, loops, functions, lists and dictionaries) and want to master the language itself: how its object model and special methods work, why iterators and generators matter, how decorators, classes, dataclasses, protocols and type hints fit together, how errors and resources are handled, how professionals structure, package and test a project, how Python does concurrency (the GIL, threads, processes, asyncio and the new free-threaded builds), and how to measure and improve performance. It ends with a complete small project in idiomatic style.

To run the code yourself, install CPython from [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (or with a tool such as [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)). Python has no official online playground, but every block with a **Run** button runs right here in your browser, using [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/). Those blocks are written to work on Python 3.10 and later; the complete programs that need a newer Python or something a browser cannot do (threads, processes) were run with CPython 3.13 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output they printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Python's history and philosophy, its toolchain, and the machinery under every line you write: names and objects, the data model and its special methods, and the iteration protocol with generators and comprehensions.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Functions as objects, closures and decorators; classes, dataclasses and protocols; type hints with a static checker; and exceptions, exception groups and context managers.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Structure, package and test a real project, choose between threads, processes and asyncio, then build, test and profile a complete tool made from the standard library.
